about: The licence ledger of PRD §15.4, kept current from the code: every data source, code port, algorithm, model, service, platform and tool (items, kept by hand) and every package a lock file pins (packages, written by docs/ledger/ledger.py build). THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES is to be generated from it at M5 (PLAN.md). licences.md is the short reading of it; data-flows.md is the data-flow inventory of PRD §15.2.

commands.check: python3 -I -B docs/ledger/ledger.py check  (every package of every lock file git tracks is here at its version, and no other; reads lock files only; an untracked lock file is named in a note and not read, and a tracked one missing on disk pins nothing)
commands.build: python3 -I -B docs/ledger/ledger.py build  (re-read the tracked lock files and the installed packages' licences, and generate each package's duty and confirm_with; keeps items, vocabulary, licence_overrides and reviewed disagreements; names untracked and missing lock files in a note, as check does)

ships.app: inside the macOS app (from M1): its binary, its webview bundle, or the data it carries (forecast files, Tier 0 frames, plates)
ships.workers: inside the capture and forecast workers: the local snapshot loops today, the Lambda image once AWS is applied
ships.eval-only: evaluation on this Mac (scores, the backtest, headless renders, the ephemeris validation); never in the app or the workers
ships.not-shipped: build tools, the M1 platform spike, the plate builder, infrastructure tooling and CI: used to make or check things, never distributed

vocabulary.ships_note: For a hosted model or a service, ships says where its calls are made from or its outputs are used.

status.confirmed: settled: the licence, basis or terms were read on this machine from the item's own files, or it is a US-government work, or the owner accepted it (PRD §1, D-012); and it agrees with THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES where they name it
status.to-confirm: not read here, or read and not settled; confirm_with says who settles it
status.planned: named in the PRD or PLAN.md, not in the code yet; its licence or terms are read before it lands
status.excluded: ruled out by the PRD or a decision

vocabulary.inclusion: Items list every outside source of what the repository runs, ships or plans: data, code ported from elsewhere, models, services, platforms, tools, packages outside any lock file, and every algorithm, formula or method the code names, in its comments, docstrings and READMEs. A method the code takes from a specific work (a paper, a book, an author's published constants or another implementation) gets its own item with that work; a standard's model that the code takes with its paper or book counts, such as the IAU 1976 precession (Lieske et al. 1977, through Meeus). The textbook techniques the code names without such a source, and the public standards whose constants and algorithms it uses as given (the WGS 84 ellipsoid, sRGB with the BT.709 and Rec. 601 luma weights, WCAG 2's contrast ratio, the CIE clear sky, SHA-256), share one item, algo.textbook-techniques. File formats, protocols, datums and identifiers (JPEG, PNG, GRIB2, HTTP, JSON Schema, ISO 8601, PEP 508, NAVD 88, EPSG codes) are not items. Every lock file's packages are in packages, written by ledger.py build.
vocabulary.duty_rule: Every entry gives its attribution duty (duty). For an item it is written by hand. For a package, ledger.py build writes it from where the package ships and its licence: 'None: not redistributed' unless it ships in the app or the workers; for the workers, none while they run only on this Mac and, once AWS is applied, in the owner's account, followed by what would apply if they were distributed; for the app, from M1, the duties of its licence expression from duty_by_licence (under OR one licence's duty is enough, under AND all apply, and an exception only adds permissions). Snow Globe's own packages point to own.snow-globe. A licence of a distributed package that duty_by_licence lacks stops the build.

duty_by_licence.0BSD: none: it asks for no notice
duty_by_licence.Apache-2.0: give recipients a copy of the licence, keep the attribution notices of any NOTICE file, and mark the files the project changed
duty_by_licence.BSD-2-Clause: reproduce the copyright notice, the conditions and the disclaimer in the documentation of a binary distribution
duty_by_licence.BSD-3-Clause: as BSD-2-Clause, and never use the authors' names to endorse the product
duty_by_licence.ISC: keep the copyright notice and the permission notice in copies
duty_by_licence.LGPL-2.1-or-later: a weak copyleft: keep its notices, and give recipients the library's source and the means to relink against a modified library
duty_by_licence.MIT: keep the copyright notice and the permission notice in all copies or substantial portions
duty_by_licence.MIT-0: none: it asks for no notice
duty_by_licence.MIT-CMU: keep the copyright notice and the permission notice in all copies and in supporting documentation
duty_by_licence.MPL-2.0: make the source of its covered files available to recipients (for unmodified files, where to get it) and keep their notices
duty_by_licence.PSF-2.0: keep the PSF's copyright notice and its licence in copies
duty_by_licence.Unicode-3.0: keep the copyright and permission notice in copies or in their documentation
duty_by_licence.Zlib: do not misrepresent the origin and mark altered sources; a binary needs no notice

vocabulary.duty_by_licence_note: Short readings of each licence's conditions for a distribution, for the M5 notices generator; the licence texts themselves govern. Every licence of a package that ships in the app or the workers must be here.

items.name: Textbook techniques and public standards that the code names without taking them from a specific work
items.licence: Textbook methods and published standards; nothing is copied from a specific work.
items.use: Techniques: Sobel and Laplacian gradients, Gaussian smoothing, Hann-tapered phase correlation and normalised cross-correlation (eval's extractor and registration, the plate builder); the capture worker's Laplacian sharpness score; Pillow's Lanczos, box and bicubic resampling (frames, thumbnails and the extractor's analysis image); bilinear and trilinear interpolation (the renderer's table lookups, the plate builder's DEM heights); Lambertian reflectance (the renderer's ground bounce and plate albedo); the Box–Muller transform in the renderer's noise; a Fisher–Yates shuffle in the core's tests; the haversine distance; bisection; least squares in the plate pose; East-North-Up frames; the normalised Levenshtein similarity, through the strsim crate; and the Ramer–Douglas–Peucker line simplification that two plate specs of the work in progress name. Public standards, whose constants and algorithms the code uses as given: the WGS 84 ellipsoid's constants (the plate builder's geodesy); sRGB's transfer curve with the BT.709 luminance weights (the renderer) and Rec. 601 luma (eval's extractor); WCAG 2's relative luminance and contrast ratio (the overlay's contrast tests); the CIE clear sky's zenith luminance (a plausibility check in a renderer test); and SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4), in the renderer's own synchronous implementation for the scene hash and seeds, and through Python's hashlib and Node's crypto elsewhere.
items.duty: None.
items.note: Listed so that every method the code names is in the ledger (vocabulary.inclusion). A technique or standard here gets its own item as soon as the code takes it from a specific work.
